alex: quick check — I'm building a small client that can send mixed inputs to the embeddings endpoint (plain string, array-of-tokens, and an explicit empty string). Three quick q's: 1) Does the API guarantee the response vectors are returned in the same order as inputs? 2) What is the behaviour for an empty string item (zero vector, omitted, error)? 3) If a single item exceeds model context length, is it truncated per-item or does the whole request fail?
jess: order should be preserved 1:1 with inputs — we don't reorder. Empty strings currently return an all-zero vector (so shape is preserved). For very long items we do per-item truncation to the model's allowed token/window. If the overall batch token budget is exceeded you'll get a 400 with code "batch_too_large".
ravi: can you paste a tiny example request/response that shows ordering + empty item behavior? helps me when I write the client tests.
alex: sure — minimal curl below (using ruf-emb-v2 as the model):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"ruf-emb-v2","input":["hello world", "", ["token1","token2"]]}'
```
expected response snippet (conceptual):
```
{ "data": [ {"embedding": [0.0,0.0,...], "index":0}, {"embedding": [0.0,0.0,...], "index":1}, {"embedding": [0.123, -0.02, ...], "index":2 } ] }
```
note: index aligns with input order.
sophie: small caveat — recent change in the SDK introduced a behavior toggle: skip_empty defaults to false now (so empty strings -> zero vectors). We debated changing it to drop empties, but that broke a few customers. @jess can confirm the default.
jess: correct — default skip_empty=false in the current release (v1.8.0). Clients can set `skip_empty=true` to have empty items omitted from the response and from the returned index mapping. When skip_empty=true we also add a `skipped_indices` array in the response to help map back.
alex: good to know. one more thing — vector dimensionality: is it stable across model minor versions? we rely on a fixed dim for storage schema.
jess: dims are stable for a given model series (ruf-emb-v2 is 1536). Minor model updates won't change dim but a major model upgrade (e.g., ruf-emb-v2 -> ruf-emb-v3) could. We publish dims in the model catalog and expose `model_details.dim` on the metadata endpoint.
ravi: thanks — i'll add tests: assert response.data.length == request.input.length when skip_empty=false, and assert each embedding.length == model_dim.
alex: and fast follow Q — how do we handle mixed-type inputs with nested arrays? e.g., sending token arrays vs strings, we just canonicalize them server-side right? no extra reordering.
jess: yes, we canonicalize to tokens internally, no reordering. We preserve `index` in the response to be explicit. For large arrays we also return `batch_token_count` in the response headers for observability.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: embeddings-service v1.8.0 -> production :white_check_mark:
sophie: awesome. tagging this thread into the release notes PR — will add a line about skip_empty default and the `skipped_indices` helper. :thumbsup:
jess: recap: order preserved, empty -> zero vector by default, per-item truncation, batch token budget error on global exceed, dims stable per model series. i'll add a short doc blurb in /docs/api/embeddings.md and link it in the release notes.
alex: perfect, thanks all. I'll update the client tests and ping when the PR is up.
